subject: chemistry
title: Subatomic particles and the size of atoms
key_idea: An atom has a tiny nucleus of **protons** and **neutrons**, surrounded by **electrons**. It has no overall charge because it has equal numbers of protons and electrons. Most of its mass is in the nucleus. Atoms are about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m in radius.

blocks.text: Every atom is made of three types of subatomic particle. This section covers where they are, their charges and their masses.

items.meaning: The tiny centre of the atom. It contains the protons and neutrons.
A positively charged particle in the nucleus.
A particle in the nucleus with no charge.
A negatively charged particle that moves around the nucleus in shells.
The number of protons in an atom of an element.

diagram.alt: Tap a part of the atom to learn its charge, mass and position, then test yourself.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.detail: The tiny centre of the atom. It is positively charged and contains the protons and neutrons.

parts.name: Proton
parts.detail: Relative charge +1 and relative mass 1. It is in the nucleus. The number of protons is the atomic number.

parts.name: Neutron
parts.detail: Relative charge 0 and relative mass 1. It is in the nucleus.

parts.name: Electron
parts.detail: Relative charge −1 and a very small relative mass (0.0005). Electrons move around the nucleus.

parts.name: Electron shells
parts.detail: The electrons are arranged in shells (energy levels) at set distances from the nucleus.

blocks.text: Why an atom has no overall charge

items: The number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
The charges +1 and −1 cancel, so the atom is neutral.
All atoms of one element have the same number of protons.
Atoms of different elements have different numbers of protons.
Protons (+1) and neutrons (0) are in the nucleus. Electrons (−1) are in shells around it.
An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so it is neutral.
The number of protons decides which element an atom is.

sections.heading: Size and mass of an atom

blocks.text: The nucleus is very small compared with the whole atom, but it holds almost all of the mass.

items: The radius of an atom is about 0.1 nm, which is 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
The radius of the nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom.
Most of an atom is empty space.
A bond length is also about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Small molecules are a little bigger, about 1 × 10⁻⁹ m across.
In order of size, smallest first: proton, atom, molecule, nanoparticle.
Most of the mass is in the nucleus, because protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1.
An electron has a very small relative mass, so the electrons add almost nothing to the mass of the atom.

rows: Width of an atom (twice the radius)

blocks.label: How many atoms fit across a width
blocks.formula: number of atoms = width of sample ÷ width of one atom
where: Both widths must be in the same unit, such as metres.
The width of an atom is twice its radius.

items.text: A sample is 2.0 mm wide. 2.0 mm = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m.
An atom with radius 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m is 2 × 10⁻¹⁰ m wide.

items: An atom has a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. The nucleus is much smaller still.
Most of the mass is in the nucleus because electrons have very little mass.
Put both sizes in the same unit before you divide.

checks.q: State the relative charge and relative mass of a neutron.
Explain why an atom has no overall electrical charge.
checks.a: It has the same number of protons (positive) as electrons (negative), so the charges cancel.

checks.q: Explain why most of the mass of an atom is in the nucleus.
checks.a: Protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1. Electrons have a very small relative mass (0.0005).

worked_example.question:
The model of the atom used today has three subatomic particles: electrons, neutrons and protons.

Complete the sentences.

Atoms of the same element have the same atomic number because they have the same number of ____.

Atoms of the same element can have different mass numbers because they have different numbers of ____.

Atoms have no overall charge because they have the same number of ____ and ____.
answer_points: Protons and electrons, in either order
worked_example.tip: One mark for each sentence. Atomic number depends only on protons, and mass number also depends on neutrons.

worked_example.question:
Atoms, molecules, nanoparticles and protons are types of particle.

List these four types of particle in order of size from smallest to largest.
answer_points: Proton, atom, molecule, nanoparticle in the correct order.
worked_example.tip: Put the particles in order of size, smallest first. The correct order scores 2 marks.

worked_example.question:
Most of the mass of an atom is in the nucleus.

Explain why.
answer_points: The relative mass of protons and neutrons is 1.
The relative mass of electrons is 0.0005, or very small in comparison.
worked_example.tip: Compare the particles in the nucleus with the electrons, using relative masses.
